title: Quarterly roadmap: Dedicated capacity orchestration & autoscale cadence
creator: Maya Chen
description: Purpose: Define and land the quarterly roadmap and operational cadence for Dedicated capacity orchestration and autoscaling. This ticket captures milestones, success metrics, trade-offs, and the cross-functional plan to move from pilot autoscale behavior to a predictable production cadence for reserved pools. Primary outcomes: 1) documented orchestration cadence (forecast -> reservation -> autoscale windows), 2) rollout checklist for pilot customers, 3) telemetry and alerts to assess economic and latency SLAs, 4) governance & guardrails for burst vs. reservation decisions.
acceptance_criteria:
- Orchestration cadence doc approved by Eng, Infra, Finance and Sales leads.
- Pilot checklist with 3 internal customers executed and results logged.
- Telemetry dashboard (utilization, p95/p99 latency, cost-per-token) available in Console beta workspace.
- Runbook for rollback and capacity hedging published.
- Stakeholder signoff (SRE, Billing, Compliance).
success_metrics:
- Pool utilization target: 55% average during business hours for committed pools.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 120ms, p99 < 400ms for reserved fast-path.
- Cost metric: effective cost-per-1M-tokens for reserved pools <= 70% of on-demand baseline.
- Autoscale correctness: <2% failed autoscale triggers in pilot.
- Customer satisfaction: NPS delta +6 for pilot customers after GA.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Over-committing capacity increases committed spend. Mitigation: implement reservation hedging and weekly forecast windows.
- Risk: Autoscale thrash (frequent up/down). Mitigation: cooldown timers, hysteresis, and a conservative initial scaling factor.
- Risk: Observability blindspots. Mitigation: include token-level cost attribution, per-pool trace sampling during pilot.
- Risk: Billing reconciliation edge cases for burst credits. Mitigation: finance-led validation script and manual audit step in pilot acceptance.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Week 0-3): finalize cadence doc and guardrails; implement telemetry skeleton. Phase 1 (Week 4-6): internal pilot with 3 Redwood teams (Console, SDK, Dedicated Ops) using canary pools. Phase 2 (Week 7-10): invite 2 early customers for private pilot; collect latency/cost telemetry and runbook exercises. Phase 3 (Week 11-13): GA feature flags, launch notes, and enablement sessions for Sales/Support. Post-GA (Week 14+): iterate on autoscale thresholds and reservation recommendations based on usage patterns.
